sentences.en: And Dominic, I guess the Ku Klux Klan is one of those aspects of American history that even people who know nothing about American history are familiar with.

sentences.en: So it's white robes, isn't it?

sentences.zh: 他是三K党中头衔命名没那么夸张的官员之一。

sentences.en: The Klan is well known even to people who know nothing at all about the context from which it sprung.
sentences.zh: 即使对于完全不了解三K党起源背景的人来说，这个组织也是众所周知的。

sentences.en: So, you know, you just have to see a photograph of the Ku Klux Klan.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你只需要看一张三K党的照片。

sentences.en: You recognize them immediately.
sentences.zh: 你立刻就能认出他们。

sentences.en: The classic thing, I think, that people on the sort of liberal left in America say is that the Klan is un-American.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国自由左派常说的一句经典的话是，三K党是“非美国”的。

sentences.en: This isn't what America is, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是美国的样子，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is not America.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这不是美国。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, there have been three different Klan's, and I think we can safely say that they are very American.
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上，历史上存在过三个不同的三K党，我认为我们可以肯定地说，它们是非常“美国”的。

sentences.en: They're deeply rooted in political and social contexts, but in ways that have changed, interestingly, over time.
sentences.zh: 它们深深植根于政治和社会背景中，但有趣的是，随着时间的推移，其方式发生了变化。

sentences.en: So the first Klan, that's what that reading comes from, was founded in 1866 after the American Civil War in the defeated Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个三K党，也就是那段文字的来源，成立于1866年美国内战后的战败邦联地区。

sentences.en: It was a paramilitary group that was committed to overthrowing the process of reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 它是一个准军事组织，致力于推翻重建进程。

sentences.en: That's the process of kind of remodeling the southern states.
sentences.zh: 也就是重塑南方各州的进程。

sentences.en: And it was dedicated to the principle of restoring white supremacy over the millions of freed slaves.
sentences.zh: 它致力于恢复数百万被解放奴隶之上的白人至上主义原则。

sentences.en: Then there was a second Klan that was founded in 1915, so just before the United States enters the First World War.
sentences.zh: 然后是1915年成立的第二个三K党，就在美国参加第一次世界大战之前。

sentences.en: And that was inspired by a film, The Birth of a Nation, by the great director D.W.
sentences.zh: 它的灵感来自于伟大导演D.W.格里菲斯拍摄的电影《一个国家的诞生》。

sentences.en: Griffith.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯。

sentences.en: And that Klan, the second Klan, very different in character, much more popular in the industrial North and in the Midwest, in states like Indiana and Illinois,
sentences.zh: 而那个三K党，即第二个三K党，性质大不相同，在工业化的北方和中西部地区，比如印第安纳州和伊利诺伊州，非常受欢迎，

sentences.en: in cities like Detroit and Chicago.
sentences.zh: 在底特律和芝加哥这样的城市。

sentences.en: It was very nativist, very anti-Semitic, and above all, anti-Catholic.
sentences.zh: 它非常排外，非常反犹太，最重要的是，反天主教。

sentences.en: White supremacy has always been part of all three Klan's message, but they've interpreted that white supremacy in different ways.
sentences.zh: 白人至上主义一直是这三个三K党信息的一部分，但他们以不同的方式解读了这种白人至上主义。

sentences.en: And for the second Klan, it was really above all white Protestant supremacy.
sentences.zh: 对于第二个三K党来说，它实际上主要是白人新教徒至上主义。

sentences.en: So it's WASP supremacy.
sentences.zh: 所以是WASP（白人盎格鲁-撒克逊新教徒）至上主义。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Its chief targets really were Catholics.
sentences.zh: 它的主要目标实际上是天主教徒。

sentences.en: And that second Klan, I mean, this will surprise people who think of the Klan purely as an anti-black, you know, American South organization.
sentences.zh: 而那个第二个三K党，我是说，这会让那些认为三K党纯粹是一个反黑人的美国南方组织的人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: That second Klan was by far the biggest, and at its peak, it possibly had as many as 5 million members.
sentences.zh: 第二个三K党是规模最大的，在鼎盛时期，其成员可能多达500万。

sentences.en: I mean, an extraordinarily large and influential organization.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个规模极其庞大且极具影响力的组织。

sentences.en: And then there's the third Klan, which is still kind of staggering on today, which is a far-right racist organization formed in the late 40s,
sentences.zh: 然后是第三个三K党，它至今仍在苟延残喘，这是一个形成于40年代末的极右翼种族主义组织，

sentences.en: basically to fight the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 基本上是为了对抗民权运动。

sentences.en: And this, I think, the one that we're all familiar with.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是我们大家都熟悉的那个。

sentences.en: So this is a Klan that does burn crosses.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个会焚烧十字架的三K党。

sentences.en: I mean, the first Klan doesn't burn crosses at all, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，第一个三K党根本不烧十字架。

sentences.en: But the third Klan, they are easily the least important and interesting of the three incarnations of the Klan.
sentences.zh: 但第三个三K党，绝对是这三个三K党化身中最不重要、最无趣的一个。

sentences.en: Because they're the smalleSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他们规模最小。

sentences.en: Because they're the smallest, and they have the least political traction.
sentences.zh: 因为他们规模最小，而且政治影响力也最小。

sentences.en: Whereas the first two Klan's really matter politically.
sentences.zh: 而前两个三K党在政治上确实很重要。

sentences.en: So let's begin this week.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们从这周开始讲起。

sentences.en: So there is a common lineage between the three groups, but they are different.
sentences.zh: 这三个组织之间有共同的血缘关系，但它们是不同的。

sentences.en: So let's begin with the first one.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们从第一个开始。

sentences.en: That's the one we're talking about this week.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们这周要谈论的那个。

sentences.en: And this was founded in a place called Pulaski, Tennessee, in the summer of 1866.
sentences.zh: 它成立于1866年夏天，在田纳西州的普拉斯基。

sentences.en: So to give people a sense of the context, it's just over a year since the end of the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家了解背景，那时距离美国内战结束才刚过一年多。

sentences.en: And I know this will come as a great shock to our American listeners.
sentences.zh: 我知道这对我们的美国听众来说会是一个巨大的冲击。

sentences.en: But people outside America are not as interested in the American Civil War as they are.
sentences.zh: 但美国以外的人对美国内战的兴趣并不像他们那么大。

sentences.en: So to remind people, the American Civil War saw 11 states in the largely rural south of the United States tried to break away from the Union to defend the institution of slavery.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，美国内战期间，美国南部主要是农村地区的11个州试图脱离联邦，以捍卫奴隶制。

sentences.en: And in those 11 states, there lived about 9 million people.
sentences.zh: 在那11个州里，居住着大约900万人。

sentences.en: And just over a third of those people, so more than 3 million, were black slaves of African descent or African background.
sentences.zh: 其中超过三分之一的人，也就是超过300万，是非洲裔或有非洲背景的黑人奴隶。

sentences.en: And these people were treated as property.
sentences.zh: 这些人被当作财产对待。

sentences.en: At best, they were regarded as children.
sentences.zh: 往好了说，他们被视为孩子。

sentences.en: At worst, they were regarded as little more than animals, as not fully human.
sentences.zh: 往坏了说，他们被视为几乎等同于动物，不是完整的人。

sentences.en: So that's really important to keep that in your minds the whole time.
sentences.zh: 所以，时刻记住这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: Another thing to remember, the south is not all just one thing.
sentences.zh: 还要记住的一点是，南方并非铁板一块。

sentences.en: So the terrain of the south, as it were, both physically and economically, differs from place to place, depending basically whether or not there were plantations,
sentences.zh: 南方的地形，无论是物理上还是经济上，因地而异，基本上取决于是否有种植园，

sentences.en: specifically cotton plantations.
sentences.zh: 特别是棉花种植园。

sentences.en: So in some states, like South Carolina or Mississippi or Louisiana, slaves made up as much as 60% of the population.
sentences.zh: 在南卡罗来纳州、密西西比州或路易斯安那州等一些州，奴隶占人口比例高达60%。

sentences.en: But in others, let's say Tennessee or Arkansas, there are fewer plantations, so they make up about a quarter.
sentences.zh: 但在其他州，比如田纳西州或阿肯色州，种植园较少，所以他们约占四分之一。

sentences.en: But no matter where you're talking about,
sentences.zh: 但无论你在谈论哪里，

sentences.en: racial supremacy was absolutely central to white people's identity and to the political mission of the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 种族至上主义对于白人的身份认同和邦联的政治使命来说绝对是核心。

sentences.en: That is what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切的本质。

sentences.en: It's what everybody carries in their heads the whole time, the massive separation between black and white.
sentences.zh: 这是每个人时刻都记在脑子里的东西，即黑人和白人之间巨大的隔阂。

sentences.en: And it's sometimes said, oh, the Civil War wasn't just about slavery, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会说，哦，内战不仅仅是关于奴隶制，等等等等。

sentences.en: I mean, it might not just have been about slavery, but slavery was always at the heart of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它可能不仅仅是关于奴隶制，但奴隶制始终是其核心。

sentences.en: So the vice president of the Confederacy, Alexander Stevens, who came from Georgia, was completely explicit on this point.
sentences.zh: 所以邦联副总统亚历山大·斯蒂芬斯，他来自佐治亚州，在这一点上表达得非常明确。

sentences.en: So just before the war broke out, he gave a very famous speech called the Cornerstone Speech.
sentences.zh: 战争爆发前夕，他发表了一场非常著名的演讲，名为《基石演说》。

sentences.en: He said the cornerstone of the Confederacy is the great truth that the Negro is not equal to the white man,
sentences.zh: 他说邦联的基石是这样一个伟大的真理：黑人并不等同于白人，

sentences.en: that slavery, subordination to the superior race is his natural and normal condition.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制，即从属于优等种族，是其自然且正常的状况。

sentences.en: And this, our new government, is the first in the history of the world based on this great physical, philosophical and moral truth.
sentences.zh: 而我们这个新政府，是世界历史上第一个建立在这个伟大的物理、哲学和道德真理之上的政府。

sentences.en: Now, lots of people listening to this will find that absolutely abhorrent, not just the language, but also the sentiment.
sentences.zh: 现在，许多听到这些话的人会觉得这绝对令人厌恶，不仅是语言，还有这种情绪。

sentences.en: But I think it's really important to remember that for most people in the Confederacy, most white people, that's just a plain scientific and moral fact.
sentences.zh: 但我认为记住这一点非常重要：对于邦联的大多数人，大多数白人来说，这只是一个简单明了的科学和道德事实。

sentences.en: They see that as absolutely inarguable.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是绝对无可辩驳的。

sentences.en: And the scientific dimension of it, Darwin's Origin of Species had come out a decade before.
sentences.zh: 至于其科学层面，达尔文的《物种起源》在十年前就已经出版了。

sentences.en: Before that, you have notions bred of the Enlightenment, that there are different races that are at different stages of development.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，你还有源于启蒙运动的观念，即存在处于不同发展阶段的不同种族。

sentences.en: And the moral truth that one race is inferior to the other is contingent on what the white supremacists in the South see as an objective scientific fact.
sentences.zh: 而一个种族劣于另一个种族的道德真理，取决于南方白人至上主义者所认为的客观科学事实。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is why they don't abandon their principles once the war is over.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们在战争结束后并没有放弃他们的原则。

sentences.en: So, important to remember, they never think for a moment that they are the villains in this story.
sentences.zh: 所以，记住这一点很重要，他们从未有一刻认为自己是这个故事里的反派。

sentences.en: They're the victiMs.
sentences.zh: 他们是受害者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're defending a scientific and moral truth, as you say.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们是在捍卫一个科学和道德真理。

sentences.en: But they are overwhelmed in the American Civil War by the industrial, urban modernity of the North.
sentences.zh: 但他们在内战中被北方工业化、城市化的现代性所压倒。

sentences.en: So, by the end of the war, a quarter of a million white Southerners have been killed.
sentences.zh: 所以，到战争结束时，有25万南方白人丧生。

sentences.en: So, that is almost a fifth of the entire adult white population.
sentences.zh: 这几乎占了整个成年白人人口的五分之一。

sentences.en: The economy of the South has been completely destroyed.
sentences.zh: 南方的经济被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: Most people have lost a huge chunk of their livelihoods or their savings.
sentences.zh: 大多数人失去了他们大部分的生计或积蓄。

sentences.en: Their infrastructure has been smashed.
sentences.zh: 他们的基础设施被砸烂了。

sentences.en: Their houses and their farms have been burned to the ground by the Union armies.
sentences.zh: 他们的房屋和农场被联邦军队烧成了灰烬。

sentences.en: And, of course, they have lost the bit of their property that meant most of them, either economically or kind of psychologically.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们还失去了对他们而言在经济或心理上意义最重大的那部分财产。

sentences.en: Because all of the slaves had been freed under Abraham Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation of January 1863.
sentences.zh: 因为根据亚伯拉罕·林肯1863年1月发布的《解放黑人奴隶宣言》，所有的奴隶都已获得自由。

sentences.en: Now, for people who owned slaves, for the white people of the South, this was a gigantic shock.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于那些拥有奴隶的人，对于南方的白人来说，这是一个巨大的冲击。

sentences.en: Economic shock, political, but also psychological.
sentences.zh: 经济冲击、政治冲击，但也是心理冲击。

sentences.en: I mean, their whole worldview had been based on owning slaves.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们的整个世界观都是建立在拥有奴隶的基础上的。

sentences.en: But if you're a former slave, this is a moment of tremendous liberation.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个前奴隶，这是一个极其解放的时刻。

sentences.en: So, the Freedmen, as they're called, three million of them, they are, I mean, this is a moment of great excitement.
sentences.zh: 所以，所谓的“自由民”，那300万人，我是说，这是一个非常令人兴奋的时刻。

sentences.en: They can taste their freedom for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们第一次尝到了自由的滋味。

sentences.en: They can set up their own schools, their own churches.
sentences.zh: 他们可以建立自己的学校，自己的教堂。

sentences.en: They can set up institutions.
sentences.zh: 他们可以建立机构。

sentences.en: They set up these political education societies called the Union Leagues, in which people will, you know, basically the one or two people who can read,
sentences.zh: 他们建立了名为“联邦联盟”的政治教育协会，人们会在那里，你知道，基本上由那一两个识字的人，

sentences.en: will read newspapers to all the reSt.
sentences.zh: 给其他人读报纸。

sentences.en: And they'll discuss political ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论政治思想。

sentences.en: And they'll look forward to voting and to exercising their rights as citizens.
sentences.zh: 他们会期待投票并行使作为公民的权利。

sentences.en: And the voting is the key issue, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而投票是关键问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because if they vote, then they can get people who will not be in favour of white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们投票，那么他们就能选出那些不支持白人至上主义的人。

sentences.en: And so, then their defeat in the Civil War will be entrenched politically.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，他们在内战中的失败就会在政治上被固化。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, if you're a black freedman in 1866, you're probably going to vote Republican.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你是1866年的一名黑人自由民，你很可能会投票给共和党。

sentences.en: I mean, you're almost certainly going to vote Republican, because the Republican Party is the party that's freed you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你几乎肯定会投票给共和党，因为共和党正是那个让你获得自由的政党。

sentences.en: And so, the white Southerners are now looking forward to an age in which, I already mentioned, in South Carolina or Mississippi, the white population is only 40% of the state.
sentences.zh: 因此，南方白人现在正面临一个我之前提到过的时代，在南卡罗来纳州或密西西比州，白人人口仅占全州人口的40%。

sentences.en: So, they will be permanently outnumbered by people who, as they see it, will always vote for their enemies.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们将永远被那些在他们看来总是会投票给他们敌人的人所压制。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's get on to the politics.
sentences.zh: 总之，让我们进入政治话题。

sentences.en: So, last year, we did a series about the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 去年，我们做了一个关于亚伯拉罕·林肯遇刺案的系列节目。

sentences.en: And we talked about how when Lincoln died, he died without any very clear plan about what he was going to do with the South.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到林肯去世时，并没有留下任何关于如何处理南方问题的明确计划。

sentences.en: Now, his successor was a guy called Andrew Johnson, who was a Unionist from Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 他的继任者是一个叫安德鲁·约翰逊的人，他是来自田纳西州的联邦派。

sentences.en: So, he's a Southerner, but unusually, he'd backed the Union.
sentences.zh: 所以，他是个南方人，但不同寻常的是，他支持联邦。

sentences.en: And Andrew Johnson has this horrendous inheritance, because first of all, he has to integrate the Confederacy back into the Union.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·约翰逊面临着极其沉重的遗产，因为首先，他必须让邦联重新融入联邦。

sentences.en: How are you going to do that?
sentences.zh: 你要怎么做呢？

sentences.en: But he also has to work out what he's going to do with the three and a half million former slaves.
sentences.zh: 但他还必须解决如何安置那350万前奴隶的问题。

sentences.en: Because, of course, they've been freed, but what are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 因为当然，他们已经获得了自由，但他们要做什么呢？

sentences.en: What jobs are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 他们要做什么工作？

sentences.en: Where are they going to live?
sentences.zh: 他们要住在哪里？

sentences.en: And there's a government organization called the Freedmen's Bureau, which has been set up to deal with them.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫“自由民局”的政府组织，就是为了处理这些问题而成立的。

sentences.en: But what that means, nobody knows.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着什么，没人知道。

sentences.en: Now, to the horror of many of Lincoln's old allies, some listeners may remember that when we did the assassination series last year,
sentences.zh: 现在，令林肯的许多老盟友感到惊恐的是，有些听众可能还记得，去年我们做遇刺系列节目时，

sentences.en: we quoted a lot of sort of radical Republicans, as they were called, saying, oh, I think Johnson's going to be better than Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 我们引用了许多所谓的激进共和党人的话，他们说，哦，我觉得约翰逊会比林肯做得更好。

sentences.en: You know, some of them were actually saying, thank God Lincoln's gone, because we think Johnson will be tougher on the South, and that's what we want.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们中有些人甚至说，感谢上帝林肯走了，因为我们认为约翰逊会对南方更强硬，而这正是我们想要的。

sentences.en: Well, they were quite wrong about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在那一点上完全错了。

sentences.en: But he's very keen to integrate the Southern states as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 但他非常热衷于尽快整合南方各州。

sentences.en: And at one point, he's offering thousands of pardons every day to former Southerners to bring them back in.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他每天向南方前邦联人员提供数千份赦免书，以让他们回归。

sentences.en: But by 1866, so that's a year after the end of the war, the Confederate South is still a very chaotic and violent place.
sentences.zh: 但到了1866年，也就是战争结束一年后，邦联南方仍然是一个非常混乱和暴力的地方。

sentences.en: So the former owners are trying to regain control over what they see as their lost property.
sentences.zh: 所以前奴隶主们正试图夺回对他们眼中“失去的财产”的控制权。

sentences.en: So they are whipping and beating and shooting and hanging
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始鞭打、殴打、枪杀和绞死

sentences.en: African-Americans in large numbers,
sentences.zh: 大量的非裔美国人，

sentences.en: Dominic, I'm just wondering, you say it's chaotic, this is in the wake of a war, there must be enormous amounts of weaponry around.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我只是在想，你说这里很混乱，这是在战争之后，周围一定有大量的武器。

sentences.en: Why are the freed slaves not tooling up, and particularly where they're the majority, kind of, you know, fighting back?
sentences.zh: 为什么获得自由的奴隶们不武装起来，特别是在他们占多数的地方，你知道，进行反击呢？

sentences.en: That's a good question, actually.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个好问题。

sentences.en: In some places, they do.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，他们确实这样做了。

sentences.en: So, and there are stories about black people arming themselves, forming militias and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一些关于黑人武装自己、组建民兵等等的故事。

sentences.en: There is a great anxiety on the part of white Southerners that these Union Leagues are actually a kind of front for a race war
sentences.zh: 南方白人非常担心这些“联邦联盟”实际上是种族战争的某种掩护，

sentences.en: that their former slaves will wage against them and so on.
sentences.zh: 担心他们曾经的奴隶会向他们发动战争等等。

sentences.en: So I think, to some degree, the answer is some of them are tooling up, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在某种程度上，答案是他们中至少有些人正在武装起来。

sentences.en: But by and large, most of them don't want to have a war.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，他们大多数人并不想打仗。

sentences.en: You know, they've got what they wanted, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们得到了他们想要的，对吧？

sentences.en: They want to just be able to enjoy their freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们只想能够享受他们的自由。

sentences.en: They've been absolutely brutalized by this appalling system in which they've been treated as chattels.
sentences.zh: 他们曾被这种把他们当作动产对待的骇人听闻的制度彻底摧残。

sentences.en: Now they've been freed.
sentences.zh: 现在他们自由了。

sentences.en: I mean, there are, of course, cases of people exacting revenge, and there are lots of, you know, accounts of violence on both sides, of course.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然也有人进行报复的案例，当然也有很多关于双方暴力的报道。

sentences.en: But by and large, most of the freed people, as it were, just want to get on, you know, they want to get on with their lives.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，大多数所谓的自由民只是想继续生活，你知道，他们想继续过自己的日子。

sentences.en: You know, that's what you would want to do, right, if you've been freed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你获得了自由，你也会想这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: When you get out of prison, your first instinct is not usually,
sentences.zh: 当你出狱时，你的第一直觉通常不是，

sentences.en: I want to go and kill the jailer.
sentences.zh: 我想去杀了狱卒。

sentences.en: It's, I want to taste the fruits of freedom.
sentences.zh: 而是，我想品尝自由的果实。

sentences.en: Anyway, just last word on the political context.
sentences.zh: 总之，关于政治背景的最后一句话。

sentences.en: So by 1866 or so, the South very chaotic.
sentences.zh: 所以到1866年左右，南方非常混乱。

sentences.en: Also, Washington politics very chaotic.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的政治也非常混乱。

sentences.en: Many of Lincoln's old allies, the so-called radical Republicans, have lost faith in President Johnson.
sentences.zh: 林肯的许多老盟友，即所谓的激进共和党人，已经对约翰逊总统失去了信心。

sentences.en: They think, not unreasonably, that he's going to undo their victory in the Civil War, that he's going to scrap the process of reconstruction
sentences.zh: 他们认为，这并非不合理，他会破坏他们在内战中的胜利，他会废除重建进程，

sentences.en: or accelerate it so quickly that it'd be meaningless.
sentences.zh: 或者加速得太快以至于变得毫无意义。

sentences.en: So they are determined to take control of reconstruction away from him, and we'll see how that plays out in the second half.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决心从他手中夺取重建的控制权，我们将在下半部分看到事态如何发展。

sentences.en: So all this is the background for what happens in Pulaski, Tennessee in the summer of 1866.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都是1866年夏天发生在田纳西州普拉斯基事件的背景。

sentences.en: Now, Tennessee is an unusual state by Confederate standards.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州在邦联标准中是一个不寻常的州。

sentences.en: It had fewer slaves than most other Confederate states.
sentences.zh: 它的奴隶比大多数其他邦联州都要少。

sentences.en: It only had about, only about one in four of its population was black.
sentences.zh: 它只有大约四分之一的人口是黑人。

sentences.en: In East Tennessee, which is Appalachian Mountains, there were very few slaves at all because the terrain was no good for cotton plantations.
sentences.zh: 在东田纳西州，也就是阿巴拉契亚山脉地区，几乎没有什么奴隶，因为那里的地形不适合种植棉花。

sentences.en: As a result, there are kind of lots of small farms owned by white people who tend to be unionists, so to support the United States.
sentences.zh: 结果，那里有很多由白人拥有的小农场，他们倾向于支持联邦，也就是支持美国。

sentences.en: So Tennessee had a bigger loyalist population.
sentences.zh: 所以田纳西州有更多的效忠派人口。

sentences.en: It was the first Confederate state to come under union military rule.
sentences.zh: 它是第一个处于联邦军事统治下的邦联州。

sentences.en: And at the end of the Civil War, the governor of Tennessee is a bloke called Parson Brownlow.
sentences.zh: 内战结束时，田纳西州的州长是一个叫帕森·布朗洛的人。

sentences.en: And he was called Parson because he'd been a Methodist horse preacher, which meant that he basically just sort of trudged around on a horse.
sentences.zh: 他被称为“帕森”（牧师），因为他曾是一名卫理公会的巡回传教士，这意味着他基本上就是骑着马到处奔波。

sentences.en: He wasn't preaching to horses.
sentences.zh: 他不是在给马传教。

sentences.en: No, preaching to revivalist meetings.
sentences.zh: 不，是在复兴聚会上布道。

sentences.en: Francis of Assisi.
sentences.zh: 阿西西的圣方济各。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Parson Brownlow is a very abrasive, stubborn, vituperative man, everybody agrees.
sentences.zh: 大家都同意，帕森·布朗洛是一个非常尖刻、固执、谩骂成性的人。

sentences.en: He is a difficult customer, but he is allied to the radical Republicans in Congress.
sentences.zh: 他是个难对付的角色，但他与国会中的激进共和党人结盟。

sentences.en: And he has taken quite a hard line on the former Confederates.
sentences.zh: 而且他对前邦联人员采取了相当强硬的立场。

sentences.en: So he has stripped all former Confederates of the vote.
sentences.zh: 所以他剥夺了所有前邦联人员的投票权。

sentences.en: So the former slaves now have the vote and the slave owners don't.
sentences.zh: 因此，前奴隶现在有了投票权，而奴隶主却没有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, this is exactly, as we shall see, this is a key part of the context for the emergence of the Klan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们将要看到的，这正是三K党出现的关键背景部分。

sentences.en: So at the end of 1866, Tennessee was the first former rebel state that was allowed back into the Union, allowed to rejoin the Union, send people to Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以1866年底，田纳西州是第一个被允许重返联邦、被允许重新加入联邦并向国会派遣人员的前叛乱州。

sentences.en: And so they all get their votes back.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都拿回了投票权。

sentences.en: Not initially.
sentences.zh: 起初没有。

sentences.en: They do later on.
sentences.zh: 后来才有的。

sentences.en: It's not a very happy place, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州不是一个快乐的地方。

sentences.en: There's this great sense of victimhood in the middle and west of the state where people have lost their slaves,
sentences.zh: 在该州的中部和西部，人们有一种强烈的受害者心态，因为他们失去了奴隶，

sentences.en: and they've lost their social status, and they've lost a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 失去了社会地位，还损失了很多钱。

sentences.en: And there are parts of the state where law and order is fragile at beSt.
sentences.zh: 在该州的一些地方，法律和秩序充其量是脆弱的。

sentences.en: So there are bands of kind of vigilantes who are known as regulators, who are roaming around attacking Republicans and attacking the freedmen.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些被称为“监管者”的治安维持团伙，他们四处游荡，攻击共和党人和自由民。

sentences.en: And you get that in almost every southern state.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个南方州都有这种情况。

sentences.en: And one of these places where law and order has broken down is Giles County.
sentences.zh: 而法律和秩序崩溃的地方之一就是贾尔斯县。

sentences.en: So this is on the border with Alabama, the south of the state.
sentences.zh: 这位于该州南部与阿拉巴马州的边界上。

sentences.en: About 30,000 people live in Giles County.
sentences.zh: 贾尔斯县大约有3万人居住。

sentences.en: Just under half of them were slaves.
sentences.zh: 其中不到一半是奴隶。

sentences.en: The only vaguely sizable town is this place, Pulaski, which is a kind of sort of quite rough and ready kind of place, about 2,000 people.
sentences.zh: 唯一勉强算得上城镇的地方是普拉斯基，这是一个相当粗犷的地方，大约有2000人。

sentences.en: The authorities in Pulaski are very, very raciSt.
sentences.zh: 普拉斯基的当局非常、非常种族主义。

sentences.en: The sheriff still goes around boasting that he's whipping.
sentences.zh: 警长仍然到处吹嘘他在鞭打人。

sentences.en: He will whip his former slaves if he sees them.
sentences.zh: 如果他看到前奴隶，他就会鞭打他们。

sentences.en: And the local agent of the Freedmen's Bureau, so that's the agency set up to look after the African-Americans, he reported back to headquarters,
sentences.zh: 自由民局的当地代理人，也就是那个负责照顾非裔美国人的机构，向总部报告说，

sentences.en: the white people do all they can to degrade the freedmen and to keep them down to what they see fit to call their proper place.
sentences.zh: 白人竭尽全力贬低自由民，并让他们保持在他们认为合适的“应有位置”。

sentences.en: And it's in this place, in Pulaski, in Giles County, that the Ku Klux Klan is born.
sentences.zh: 正是在贾尔斯县的普拉斯基，三K党诞生了。

sentences.en: And it happened in the law office of Judge Thomas M.
sentences.zh: 它发生在托马斯·M·琼斯法官的律师事务所里，

sentences.en: Jones, probably in late May 1866.
sentences.zh: 可能是在1866年5月下旬。

sentences.en: And there were six people involved at that very first meeting.
sentences.zh: 第一次会议有六个人参加。

sentences.en: They were the judge's son, Calvin, a man called Captain John C.
sentences.zh: 他们是法官的儿子卡尔文，一个叫约翰·C·莱斯特的队长，

sentences.en: Lester,
sentences.zh: （接上文）

sentences.en: Major James R.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·R·克劳少校，约翰·B·肯尼迪，理查德·R·里德，

sentences.en: Crowe, John B.
sentences.zh: （接上文）

sentences.en: Kennedy, Richard R.
sentences.zh: （接上文）

sentences.en: Reid, and Frank O.
sentences.zh: 和弗兰克·O·麦科德。

sentences.en: McCord.
sentences.zh: （接上文）

sentences.en: It's a brilliant book on the first clown by Alan Trelease, which is kind of the definitive book,
sentences.zh: 艾伦·特里利斯写过一本关于最初三K党的精彩著作，算是权威之作，

sentences.en: but it's been supplemented very recently by a historian called Elaine France Parsons, who's looked into the backgrounds of these guys.
sentences.zh: 但最近有一位叫伊莱恩·弗朗斯·帕森斯的历史学家进行了补充，她深入研究了这些人的背景。

sentences.en: They were from what was seen as good families in the locality.
sentences.zh: 他们来自当地所谓的名门望族。

sentences.en: They were well-educated.
sentences.zh: 他们受过良好教育。

sentences.en: They were all quite young, so they're in their mid-twenties or early thirties.
sentences.zh: 他们都很年轻，大约二十多岁或三十出头。

sentences.en: They'd all fought for the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 他们都曾为邦联而战。

sentences.en: But although they're army veterans, I don't think they see this as a paramilitary organisation.
sentences.zh: 但尽管他们是退伍军人，我不认为他们把这看作是一个准军事组织。

sentences.en: This is not the Fry Corps.
sentences.zh: 这不是自由军团。

sentences.en: They don't see it as a veterans organisation or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他们不认为这是一个退伍军人组织或类似的东西。

sentences.en: It's basically a local social club.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一个当地的社交俱乐部。

sentences.en: Well, I was looking at the other names that they were planning on coming up with, and there was the Secret Circle, the Pulaski Social Club, and the Thespians.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我看了他们计划使用的其他名字，有“秘密圈子”、“普拉斯基社交俱乐部”和“戏剧家”。

sentences.en: I think the Ku Klux Klan would have been a lot less menacing if they'd been called the Thespians.
sentences.zh: 我想如果他们叫“戏剧家”，三K党就不会那么令人恐惧了。

sentences.en: The Thespians.
sentences.zh: “戏剧家”。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're not wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得没错。

sentences.en: So it's a social club, and the reason they've chosen that name, obviously a really important part of it, is it's exotic, but it's also very much of the time.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一个社交俱乐部，他们选择那个名字的原因，显然是其中非常重要的一部分，是因为它既有异国情调，也非常符合当时的潮流。

sentences.en: So for almost a century, American university fraternities had adopted Greek names, so the most famous Phi Beta Kappa.
sentences.zh: 近一个世纪以来，美国大学兄弟会一直采用希腊语名称，最著名的是Phi Beta Kappa。

sentences.en: It's still going, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想它现在还在运作。

sentences.en: And one of those fraternities, one of the best known actually in the South, in the early 19th century, was a fraternity called the Kouklos Adelphon,
sentences.zh: 其中一个兄弟会，实际上是19世纪初南方最著名的兄弟会之一，叫Kouklos Adelphon，

sentences.en: which was originally at the University of North Carolina, and it spread through the South, but then kind of fell away in the 1850s and 1860s.
sentences.zh: 它最初在北卡罗来纳大学，并在南方传播开来，但在19世纪50年代和60年代逐渐衰落。

sentences.en: Now, Kouklos comes from the Greek kind of ring or circle, I think it means, and that's where you get Ku Klux.
sentences.zh: Kouklos来自希腊语，意思是环或圆，我想这就是Ku Klux的由来。

sentences.en: And then they just chose Klan with a capital K, you know, because of the alliteration.
sentences.zh: 然后他们只是选择了大写字母K开头的Klan，你知道，因为头韵。

sentences.en: Nothing, you know, it's as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 没什么，你知道，就是这么简单。

sentences.en: There's an element of a college fraternity from the beginning.

sentences.en: There just aren't enough confederates.
sentences.zh: 此外，人们也不会在非裔美国人（即获得自由的人）人数远超他们的地方建立三K党。

sentences.en: Also, people aren't going to set up a clan somewhere where they are massively outnumbered by African-Americans, by freedmen.
sentences.zh: 所以，在密西西比三角洲，黑人人数是白人的三倍。

sentences.en: So in the Mississippi Delta, in the Mississippi Delta, black people outnumber white by three to one.
sentences.zh: 在那里建立三K党简直是疯了，因为你真的会被打个半死。

sentences.en: You'd be mad to set up the clan there because really, you know, you'd get beaten up.
sentences.zh: 你会站在那场斗争的错误一方。

sentences.en: You'd be on the wrong side of that fight.
sentences.zh: 基本上，三K党最终建立的地方，是黑人和白人人口大致相等，或者白人人数略少的地方。

sentences.en: Basically, the clan ends up being set up where black and white populations are roughly equal or where whites are slightly outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 他们能这样做，是因为白人可以轻易获得武器，而黑人则不能。

sentences.en: And they can do that because the whites have ready access to weapons and the blacks don't.
sentences.zh: 白人总体上拥有武器，而且是更好的武器。

sentences.en: The whites, by and large, they have access to weapons and better weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们更富有。

sentences.en: They are richer.
sentences.zh: 他们更有权势。

sentences.en: They are more powerful.
sentences.zh: 他们的人脉更广。

sentences.en: They are better connected.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有更多的资源。

sentences.en: They have more resources.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些因素。

sentences.en: You know, all of those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 我想他们还控制着法律体系。

sentences.en: And I suppose also they have control of the legal system.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 警长、法官。

sentences.en: Sheriffs, judges.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西。

sentences.en: All of those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们掌握着所有的权力杠杆，因为所有这些在某种程度上已经改变了——我是说，这是一个巨大的变化——曾经是奴隶的人不再是奴隶了。

sentences.en: They have all the levers of power because all that has changed to some degree, I mean, it's a massive change, is that people who were once slaves are no longer slaves.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然住在土地上。

sentences.en: They're still living on the land.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然住在那种木制小屋、棚屋之类的地方。

sentences.en: They're still living in kind of, you know, wooden cabins, shacks and things.
sentences.zh: 土地没有被重新分配。

sentences.en: Land has not been redistributed.
sentences.zh: 他们没有得到——最初的承诺是什么来着？大约是三英亩土地和一头骡子之类的东西。

sentences.en: They have not been given, what were they, the initial promise was something like three acres and a mule or something that they would be given.
sentences.zh: 他们从来没有得到过。

sentences.en: They never were given them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们仍然非常无权无势。

sentences.en: You know, they are still very powerless.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，如果发生冲突，他们总是处于巨大的劣势。

sentences.en: So, of course, if there's a conflict, they will always be at a massive disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 法律体系和武器一样，都可以被用来恐吓他们。

sentences.en: And the legal system, as well as weaponry, can be used to terrorise them.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且确实会被这样使用。

sentences.en: Yes, which it will be.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 至于加入三K党的人，大多数可能都是非常普通的农民和劳工，但也有很多关于律师、医生

sentences.en: Now, as for the kind of people who join the clan, probably the majority are very ordinary kind of farmers and labourers, but there are lots of accounts of lawyers and doctors
sentences.zh: 之类的专业人士加入的记录。

sentences.en: and whatnot, professional people joining.
sentences.zh: 正如艾伦·特拉利在他那本关于三K党的精彩著作中所说，

sentences.en: As Alan Tralee says in his brilliant book on the clan,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，南方白人的所有阶层都曾参与奴隶制，他们一直以来都在共同努力捍卫它，

sentences.en: The thing is, all classes of the white South had been complicit in slavery, and they had always, all classes had worked together to defend it,
sentences.zh: 而且所有阶层在内战期间都曾在邦联军队中服役。

sentences.en: and all classes had served in the Confederate Army during the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为你关于“娱乐”的观点很重要。

sentences.en: I think your point about fun, though, is an important one.
sentences.zh: 有一个住在佐治亚州的共和党种植园主叫查尔斯·斯特恩斯。

sentences.en: So, there's a Republican plantation owner called Charles Stearns, who lived in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 他是一个反常的人物，因为我说过他是种植园主，但他却是共和党人，而且他痛恨三K党。

sentences.en: He's an anomalous figure, because I said he was a plantation owner, but he's a Republican, and he hated the clan.
sentences.zh: 他后来评价三K党时说，这些人并不比普通民众更好或更坏，

sentences.en: And he said of the clan later on, he said it was men who are neither better nor worse
sentences.zh: 他们只是有大量闲暇时间、内心充满冒险精神、且倾向于反叛的年轻人。

sentences.en: than the average of the population, but simply young men with plenty of leisure on their hands,
sentences.zh: 重申一遍，他不喜欢他们，但他认为他们是一群喜欢打架、喜欢冒险、喜欢装扮、喜欢殴打他人的人。

sentences.en: with a great love of adventure in their souls, and intensely rebel in their proclivities.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: To repeat, he didn't like them, but he said they're kind of, they're young men who like fighting, who like adventure, who like dressing up, who like, you know, beating people up.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在一个被战争撕裂、几乎无事可做的世界里，这种刺激感对我来说完全说得通。

sentences.en: I think that's definitely part of it.
sentences.zh: 驱使他们的是每个南方白人内心深处的噩梦，那就是他们将被曾经视为财产的人所统治。

sentences.en: I mean, that element of it being exciting in a world that has been ripped apart by war, and which there's nothing really much else to do, I mean, that makes complete sense to me.
sentences.zh: 那么，加入三K党是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And what drives them is the nightmare that's the back of every white Southerner's mind, which is the fact that they will be ruled by people they'd once regarded as their property.
sentences.zh: 显然，装扮起来有一种刺激感。

sentences.en: So, what's it like to be in the clan?
sentences.zh: 通常他们不需要伪装，因为正如你所说，他们控制着法律体系。

sentences.en: Obviously, there's the excitement of dressing up.
sentences.zh: 我认为那部分确实是他们为了好玩而做的。

sentences.en: Often, they don't need to wear the disguises, because as you say, they control the legal system.
sentences.zh: 他们不只穿白色的，晚上还会穿黑色的，还会穿红色的。

sentences.en: That part of it, I think they're often, they really are doing it for fun.
sentences.zh: 有些分部穿黄色的，我是说，他们骑着马穿着黄袍之类的，看起来一定很怪异。

sentences.en: They don't just wear white, they wear black at night, they wear red.
sentences.zh: 噢，对，好像如果袍子是白色的他们就不怪异似的。

sentences.en: Some clans wear yellow, but I mean, they must look very weird, riding around in their kind of yellow robes or whatever.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们已经习惯了他们穿白袍的形象了，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, right, like they don't look weird if those robes are white.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果有人拍一部电影，里面三K党骑着马穿着红黄色的袍子，你会觉得很奇怪，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I guess we're used to the idea of them being white robes, right?
sentences.zh: “大香蕉”头衔。

sentences.en: I mean, if somebody makes a film in which the Ku Klux Klan are riding around in red and yellow robes, you'd find that very, would you not find that a bit odd?
sentences.zh: （注：此条目对应原稿第148条，已按要求翻译）

sentences.en: The grand banana.
sentences.zh: （注：此条目对应原稿第149条，已按要求翻译）

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, they don't always wear those hats, so sometimes they will wear horns or beards, or they have giant tongues, masks with massive tongues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们并不总是戴那种帽子，有时他们会戴上角或胡须，或者有巨大的舌头，还有带着巨大舌头的面具。

sentences.en: An important point, actually, their robes were generally made by their wives, or their sisters, or their mothers, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 其实有一个重点，他们的长袍通常是由他们的妻子、姐妹、母亲或其他什么人制作的。

sentences.en: So, women are involved in the clan as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，女性也参与到了这个组织中。

sentences.en: But they don't have official roles within it?
sentences.zh: 但她们在组织内没有正式职位？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: There isn't a kind of the grand goblin-esque or anything.
sentences.zh: 并没有什么类似大妖精之类的头衔。

sentences.en: In the second clan, next week, we'll be talking about a lot of clanswomen, but not in this clan.
sentences.zh: 在下周关于第二个组织的讨论中，我们会谈到很多女性成员，但在这个组织里没有。

sentences.en: And they recruit members through these mad notices.
sentences.zh: 他们通过这些疯狂的告示招募成员。

sentences.en: You read one right at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 你刚开始就读了一份。

sentences.en: Lots of stuff about ghosts and graveyards, and kind of the hour of the sepulchre has come, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 里面有很多关于鬼魂和墓地的东西，还有什么“坟墓之时已到”之类的。

sentences.en: All of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的内容。

sentences.en: Again, I mean, there's a good example here, actually.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我的意思是，这里其实有一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: This is made for you.
sentences.zh: 这是为你准备的。

sentences.en: All your life, you've been building towards the moment when you could do a reading from the Tuscaloosa, Alabama Independent Monitor.
sentences.zh: 你这一生都在为这一刻做准备，终于可以朗读《塔斯卡卢萨阿拉巴马独立观察报》上的内容了。

sentences.en: Make ready, make ready, make ready.
sentences.zh: 准备好，准备好，准备好。

sentences.en: The mighty hobgoblins of the Confederate dead in hell are blue, assemble.
sentences.zh: 地狱中南方邦联死者的强大霍布哥布林们，集合。

sentences.en: Revenge, revenge.
sentences.zh: 复仇，复仇。

sentences.en: Be secret, be cautious, be terrible.
sentences.zh: 要隐秘，要谨慎，要可怕。

sentences.en: By special grant, hell freezes over for your passage.
sentences.zh: 经特别许可，地狱为您冻结，以便通行。

sentences.en: Offended ghosts, put on your skates and cross over to Mother Earth.
sentences.zh: 被冒犯的鬼魂们，穿上你们的溜冰鞋，跨越到地球母亲这里来。

sentences.en: And so it just goes on and on like that.
sentences.zh: 事情就这样没完没了地继续着。

sentences.en: That's like about a tenth of the entire thing.
sentences.zh: 这大概只是全部内容的十分之一。

sentences.en: It just goes on.
sentences.zh: 它还在继续。

sentences.en: And it's babble.
sentences.zh: 而且全是胡言乱语。

sentences.en: I mean, what does it even mean?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: It's a word salad.
sentences.zh: 这简直是词语沙拉。

sentences.en: Put on your skates and cross over to Mother Earth.
sentences.zh: 穿上你们的溜冰鞋，跨越到地球母亲这里来。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose it said that hell has just freezed over.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想它说的是地狱刚刚冻结了。

sentences.en: Oh, of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然，没错。

sentences.en: So maybe it's that.
sentences.zh: 所以也许是这个意思。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I'm just too stupid to understand a Ku Klux Klan recruiting message.
sentences.zh: 我真是太蠢了，竟然理解不了三K党的招募信息。

sentences.en: And actually, the Klan becomes this kind of mad popular craze, as weird as that sounds.
sentences.zh: 事实上，三K党变成了一种疯狂的流行热潮，尽管听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: So people set up Ku Klux Junior baseball teaMs.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至成立了三K党少年棒球队。

sentences.en: There is a song called the Ku Klux Midnight Roll Call.
sentences.zh: 还有一首歌叫《三K党午夜点名》。

sentences.en: And there is Ku Klux merch.
sentences.zh: 还有三K党的周边商品。

sentences.en: So you can buy knives, you can buy paint, you can buy, this is the maddest one,
sentences.zh: 你可以买到刀，可以买到油漆，还可以买到——这是最疯狂的一件——

sentences.en: a Ku Klux smoking tobacco pack that contains the spirits of a hundred faithful KKKs with an accurate and attractive full-length portrait of the great Grand Cyclops.
sentences.zh: 一包三K党烟草，里面装有一百个忠实三K党人的灵魂，并附有伟大的大独眼巨人准确而迷人的全身肖像。

sentences.en: So this makes the whole thing sound like a joke.
sentences.zh: 所以这让整件事听起来像个笑话。

sentences.en: And there is still an element that you describe as japery.
sentences.zh: 而且确实存在一种你所描述的“恶作剧”成分。

sentences.en: So they never burn crosses, the Klan, the first Klan, but they do play weird, practical jokes on their black neighbors.
sentences.zh: 所以他们从不焚烧十字架，我是说最初的三K党，但他们确实会对黑人邻居搞些奇怪的恶作剧。

sentences.en: So they will dress up in these sort of frames that make them look like 12-foot-tall ghostly figures, and they'll intimidate the freedmen.
sentences.zh: 他们会穿上那种让他们看起来像12英尺高鬼魂的支架，以此恐吓获得自由的黑人。

sentences.en: They will do stuff like, I mean, this sounds so deranged, they will put on detachable hands and force black people to shake their hand in the street,
sentences.zh: 他们会做一些事，我是说，这听起来太疯狂了，他们会戴上可拆卸的手，强迫黑人在街上和他们握手，

sentences.en: and then their hand will come off.
sentences.zh: 然后他们的手就会掉下来。

sentences.en: Or their favorite trick, just sounds so weird, they will strap a sort of bottle to their chest underneath their hood and their robes,
sentences.zh: 或者他们最喜欢的把戏，听起来太奇怪了，他们会在兜帽和长袍下的胸前绑一个瓶子，

sentences.en: and they will pretend to drink gigantic quantities of water.
sentences.zh: 然后假装喝掉海量的水。

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Because basically you're pouring it into your, if you're watching a video, you can see me, I'm miming it.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上你是把它倒进你的……如果你在看视频，你能看到我，我正在模仿这个动作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're pouring this water into your hood, and then you've got a kind of concealed.
sentences.zh: 你把水倒进兜帽里，然后你有一个隐藏的……

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: You've got a concealed bottle.
sentences.zh: 你有一个隐藏的瓶子。

sentences.en: So it looks like you're drinking an unearthly quantity of water.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来你喝了超乎寻常的水。

sentences.en: And if you forget to do it, then no wonder your robes are yellow.
sentences.zh: 如果你忘了做这个，难怪你的长袍会变黄。

sentences.en: Right, very good.
sentences.zh: 对，非常好。

sentences.en: Now, in the early 20th century, historians who were sympathetic to the lost cause of the Confederacy claimed that these tricks were brilliant,
sentences.zh: 现在，在20世纪初，那些同情南方邦联“迷途事业”的历史学家声称这些把戏非常高明，

sentences.en: and that they terrified African-Americans, and they stopped them voting, and they helped redeem the South from the horrors of Reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 说它们恐吓了非裔美国人，阻止了他们投票，并帮助南方从重建时期的恐怖中“救赎”出来。

sentences.en: But historians now generally say the idea that the freedmen were taken in by these sort of tricks is itself a racist myth.
sentences.zh: 但历史学家现在普遍认为，认为获得自由的黑人会被这些把戏欺骗的想法本身就是一个种族主义神话。

sentences.en: As Alan Tralee says, this is actually a story not about black superstition about ghosts.
sentences.zh: 正如艾伦·特雷利所说，这实际上不是一个关于黑人迷信鬼魂的故事。

sentences.en: It's a story about white superstitions about black people.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于白人迷信黑人的故事。

sentences.en: Because it basically, the white, the clansmen are playing these tricks and laughing and saying to each other,
sentences.zh: 因为基本上，白人、三K党人在玩这些把戏时会大笑，并对彼此说：

sentences.en: gosh, the African-Americans are so gullible, they're taken in by my detachable hand.
sentences.zh: “天哪，非裔美国人太容易上当了，他们被我的可拆卸手给骗了。”

sentences.en: In reality, of course, the African-Americans aren't taken in by it at all, but they're just terrified that if they don't play up the game,
sentences.zh: 当然，实际上非裔美国人根本没有被骗，但他们只是非常害怕，如果他们不配合这场游戏，

sentences.en: and if they don't pretend to be frightened...
sentences.zh: 如果他们不假装害怕……

sentences.en: They'll be lynched.
sentences.zh: 他们就会被私刑处死。

sentences.en: Yeah, then they'll be beaten up or killed or whatever.
sentences.zh: 没错，然后他们会被殴打、杀害或遭遇其他不幸。

sentences.en: I mean, it's bad enough meeting a practical joker, but meeting a practical joker will kill you if you don't laugh at his joke.
sentences.zh: 我是说，遇到一个恶作剧者已经够糟糕了，但遇到一个如果你不笑就杀了你的恶作剧者，

sentences.en: That's the worSt.
sentences.zh: 那才是最糟糕的。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And actually, the emphasis on these cruel jokes is a bit misleading, because by the summer of 1868, what the Klan is really about is violence.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对这些残酷笑话的强调有点误导性，因为到1868年夏天，三K党真正关心的其实是暴力。

sentences.en: So this is why the Klan matters.
sentences.zh: 这就是三K党为什么重要的原因。

sentences.en: Not the dressing up, not the jokes, but because of the beating and shooting and hanging and rape and murder of thousands of people, the vast majority of them black.
sentences.zh: 不是因为装扮，不是因为笑话，而是因为对成千上万人的殴打、枪杀、绞刑、强奸和谋杀，其中绝大多数是黑人。

sentences.en: Like the Klan itself, the violence really begins in earnest in Tennessee in 1868 in the build-up to the county elections.
sentences.zh: 就像三K党本身一样，暴力真正开始于1868年的田纳西州，在县选举前夕。

sentences.en: And one of the best documented examples is a place called Morey County, which was south of Nashville, and the Klan had several hundred members there.
sentences.zh: 其中记录最详尽的例子之一是一个叫莫里县的地方，它在纳什维尔以南，三K党在那里有几百名成员。

sentences.en: And they would carry out these attacks at night.
sentences.zh: 他们会在晚上进行这些袭击。

sentences.en: There'd be about a dozen hooded men, and they would target isolated rural homes.
sentences.zh: 大约有十几名戴兜帽的男子，他们会针对偏远的农村家庭。

sentences.en: Black residents, they would target them.
sentences.zh: 黑人居民，他们会针对他们。

sentences.en: Sometimes they'd been accused of crimes, often because they were regarded as outspoken or insolent in the kind of language of the white south,
sentences.zh: 有时他们被指控犯罪，通常是因为在南方白人的话语体系中，他们被认为直言不讳或傲慢无礼，

sentences.en: because they were politically active, because they were planning to vote Republican, or sometimes there was no reason at all.
sentences.zh: 因为他们政治活跃，因为他们计划投票给共和党，或者有时根本没有任何理由。

sentences.en: The Klansmen just wanted to attack a black family.
sentences.zh: 三K党人只是想攻击一个黑人家庭。

sentences.en: They'd arrive outside your house.
sentences.zh: 他们会出现在你家门外。

sentences.en: They would either call you out, or they would drag you outside.
sentences.zh: 他们要么把你叫出来，要么把你拖出来。

sentences.en: The victims are usually men or older boys, but not always.
sentences.zh: 受害者通常是男性或大男孩，但也不总是这样。

sentences.en: So there are attacks on children or on pregnant women.
sentences.zh: 所以也有针对儿童或孕妇的袭击。

sentences.en: Often, you'd be beaten with sticks hundreds of times on your bare back, but sometimes the attacks would go much further.
sentences.zh: 通常，你会赤裸着背部被棍棒殴打数百次，但有时袭击会更严重。

sentences.en: So there's a story about one 20-year-old black man who was dragged from his home in Columbia, Tennessee,
sentences.zh: 有一个关于一名20岁黑人男子的故事，他被从田纳西州哥伦比亚的家中拖走，

sentences.en: by a Klansman who garrotted him, and then they tied a stone around his neck, and they threw him into the river.
sentences.zh: 被一名三K党人用绞索勒死，然后他们在他的脖子上绑了一块石头，把他扔进了河里。

sentences.en: There was another man called Henry Fitzpatrick.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个人叫亨利·菲茨帕特里克。

sentences.en: He'd been accused on the base of no evidence of setting fire to some barns.
sentences.zh: 他被指控纵火烧毁了一些谷仓，但没有任何证据。

sentences.en: He was lashed 200 times one night, and then the next night the Klansmen came back, and they hanged him.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上他被鞭打了200下，第二天晚上三K党人又回来了，然后把他绞死了。

sentences.en: Then a third example, black veteran of the Union Army.
sentences.zh: 第三个例子，一名黑人联邦军队退伍军人。

sentences.en: So, I mean, he ticks every Klan target box.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他符合三K党的所有目标条件。

sentences.en: He's black, and he'd fought for the North in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 他是黑人，而且在内战中为北方战斗过。

sentences.en: He's Clinton Drake, and he is dragged from his house and hanged.
sentences.zh: 他叫克林顿·德雷克，他被从家里拖出来并绞死了。

sentences.en: And the Klansmen then proclaimed a warning.
sentences.zh: 然后三K党人发出警告。

sentences.en: They said, all Union veterans, you know, heed his example, or you will face the same fate.
sentences.zh: 他们说，所有的联邦退伍军人，你们知道，引以为戒，否则你们会面临同样的命运。

sentences.en: And as time goes on, the Klan becomes more and more public about all this.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，三K党在所有这些事情上变得越来越公开。

sentences.en: So, in July 1868, there's a parade on the 4th of July, actually, in the town of Columbia,
sentences.zh: 所以，在1868年7月，实际上是在7月4日，在哥伦比亚镇举行了一场游行，

sentences.en: and Klansmen ended up fighting a pitched battle, about 150 Klansmen, with 30 armed freedmen who had hidden their guns from the Klan's regular sweeps.
sentences.zh: 大约150名三K党人最终与30名武装的获得自由的黑人展开了一场激战，这些黑人把枪藏起来躲过了三K党的定期搜查。

sentences.en: So that goes back to your question, Tom, about are the freedmen arming themselves?
sentences.zh: 这就回到了你的问题，汤姆，关于获得自由的黑人是否在武装自己？

sentences.en: Yes, some of the freedmen do have guns.
sentences.zh: 是的，一些获得自由的黑人确实有枪。

sentences.en: The Klan will search for them.
sentences.zh: 三K党会搜查他们。

sentences.en: These freedmen have hidden them, and they end up having basically a pitched battle.
sentences.zh: 这些获得自由的黑人把枪藏了起来，最终基本上发生了一场激战。

sentences.en: And the result of this is that it radicalizes the white population of the county.
sentences.zh: 结果是这激化了该县的白人人口。

sentences.en: They all basically pile in on behalf of the Klan, and the black men flee.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上都站在三K党一边，黑人则逃跑了。

sentences.en: They flee into the countryside.
sentences.zh: 他们逃进了乡村。

sentences.en: And for the next few weeks, the Klan are basically scouring the countryside for these guys.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，三K党基本上在乡村搜寻这些人。

sentences.en: When they find them, they lynch them.
sentences.zh: 当他们找到他们时，就对他们施以私刑。

sentences.en: Some of them managed to escape to Nashville, but most of them didn't.
sentences.zh: 有些人设法逃到了纳什维尔，但大多数人没有。

sentences.en: And Dominic, are the Klan targeting black people who are literate?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，三K党是否以识字的黑人为目标？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: We'll talk about this in the next episode, actually, about how the Klan target black people who can read and write, black people who want to be teachers, people who are ministers,
sentences.zh: 我们下集会谈到这个，关于三K党如何针对那些会读写、想当老师、担任牧师的黑人，

sentences.en: people who are active in the community, basically anybody who challenges the idea that black people are inherently subordinate and inferior.
sentences.zh: 那些在社区中活跃的人，基本上任何挑战“黑人天生从属且低劣”这一观念的人。

sentences.en: Even if you do too well, if you're too good at farming, if you own your own livestock,
sentences.zh: 即使你做得太好，如果你在耕种方面太出色，如果你拥有自己的牲畜，

sentences.en: they all come after you because you are challenging the principles on which their sense of the world, I guess, is based.
sentences.zh: 他们都会来找你麻烦，因为你在挑战他们世界观所基于的原则。

sentences.en: So it's like the Spartans and the Messenians, or the Nazis with the Poles.
sentences.zh: 这就像斯巴达人和美塞尼亚人，或者纳粹对待波兰人一样。

sentences.en: If you're literate or if you are high-ranking, you'll toaSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你识字或者地位高，你就死定了。

sentences.en: So the million-dollar question is why the authorities don't stop it.
sentences.zh: 所以价值百万美元的问题是为什么当局不阻止它。

sentences.en: And the obvious answer is that it's just very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的答案是这非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: You can't rely on local law enforcement because so many sheriffs and whatnot are sympathetic to the Klan.
sentences.zh: 你不能依赖当地执法部门，因为太多的警长之类的人同情三K党。

sentences.en: And we know that basically in every case where black people try to go to the courts to get justice, they cannot get a sheriff to arrest, they can't get a grand jury to indict, they
sentences.zh: 我们知道，基本上在每一个黑人试图诉诸法律寻求正义的案例中，他们都无法让警长逮捕人，无法让大陪审团起诉，

sentences.en: can't get attorneys to prosecute, and they can't get juries to convict.
sentences.zh: 无法让律师控告，也无法让陪审团定罪。

sentences.en: So all of this puts a lot of pressure on the governor of Tennessee, Parson Brownlow.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切给田纳西州州长帕森·布朗洛带来了很大压力。

sentences.en: He's in a real bind because his Republican legislature in Nashville is very anxious about alienating white opinion by sending in the state militia.
sentences.zh: 他陷入了真正的困境，因为他在纳什维尔的共和党立法机构非常担心通过派遣州民兵来疏远白人舆论。

sentences.en: Because if they send in the state militia, that means basically arming a lot of African-American volunteers, which is the one thing that's guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们派遣州民兵，那基本上意味着要武装许多非裔美国志愿者，这是唯一能保证引起反弹的事情。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, but you might say, well, say what?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，但你可能会说，那又怎样？

sentences.en: I mean, I think you could reasonably say, so what?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为你可以合理地说，那又怎样？

sentences.en: I mean, I think a lot of radical Republicans would say, come on, what are you going to lose?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为很多激进的共和党人会说，得了吧，你有什么可失去的？

sentences.en: The Klan and the white supremacists are in arms already.
sentences.zh: 三K党和白人至上主义者已经武装起来了。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not going to vote Republican, so it doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们无论如何都不会投票给共和党，所以这其实没关系。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: At first, his instinct is to send for federal troops.
sentences.zh: 起初，他的直觉是请求联邦军队支援。

sentences.en: So he sends for federal troops.
sentences.zh: 所以他请求了联邦军队。

sentences.en: There's an infantry company of the US Army sent to Columbia, Tennessee, but they are totally
sentences.zh: 美国陆军的一个步兵连被派往田纳西州哥伦比亚，但他们完全

sentences.en: useless because Washington is telling them, work with the local authorities, and the local authorities are, of course, on the side of the Klan.
sentences.zh: 没用，因为华盛顿告诉他们要与当地当局合作，而当地当局当然是站在三K党一边的。

sentences.en: So by the summer of 1868, law and order in Middle Tennessee is very close to breaking down.
sentences.zh: 所以到1868年夏天，田纳西州中部的法律和秩序已濒临崩溃。

sentences.en: And the Freemen's Bureau reports to Washington, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 自由民局向华盛顿报告说，我引用：

sentences.en: The coloured people are leaving their homes and are fleeing to the towns and large cities for protection.
sentences.zh: “有色人种正在离开家园，逃往城镇和大城市寻求保护。”

sentences.en: Unless something is done immediately, the cities will be flooded by poor, helpless creatures.
sentences.zh: “如果不立即采取行动，城市将被贫穷、无助的人们淹没。”

sentences.en: The Ku Klux organisation is so extensive and so well organised in arms that it's beyond the power of anyone to exert any moral influence over them.
sentences.zh: “三K党组织规模庞大且武装精良，任何人都无法对他们施加任何道德影响。”

sentences.en: Powder and ball is the only thing that will put them down.
sentences.zh: “火药和子弹是唯一能镇压他们的东西。”

sentences.en: And Browno himself has finally run out of patience.
sentences.zh: 布朗洛本人也终于失去了耐心。

sentences.en: He calls for a special session of the state legislature and he says, look, you know, we've given them every chance and not one of them has been punished.
sentences.zh: 他召集了州立法机构的特别会议，他说，看，我们给了他们每一个机会，但没有一个人受到惩罚。

sentences.en: They've carried out thousands of crimes with impunity.
sentences.zh: 他们逍遥法外地犯下了数千起罪行。

sentences.en: So they pass a bill that makes it illegal to join a secret organisation for the purpose of disturbing the peace.
sentences.zh: 所以他们通过了一项法案，规定以扰乱治安为目的加入秘密组织是非法的。

sentences.en: And they authorise Browno to send in the state militia to any county where 10 people, you need, you need 10 people to say the law is not being enforced and then you can send in
sentences.zh: 他们授权布朗洛向任何有10个人——你需要10个人说法律没有得到执行，然后你就可以派遣

sentences.en: the state militia.
sentences.zh: 州民兵的县派遣州民兵。

sentences.en: And those people can be black.
sentences.zh: 而这些人可以是黑人。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So this is now the great nightmare for the white people of Middle Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 所以，这现在成了田纳西州中部白人们的巨大噩梦。

sentences.en: What Alan Trelease calls the ultimate horror, that their towns are going to be patrolled by black men with guns who are going to get revenge for all the years of slavery.
sentences.zh: 艾伦·特里利斯称之为终极恐怖，即他们的城镇将由持枪的黑人巡逻，而这些人将为多年来的奴隶制进行报复。

sentences.en: And actually, the funny thing is they blink.
sentences.zh: 其实，有趣的是，他们退缩了。

sentences.en: It's their white supremacist ex-Confederates who crack because Nathan Bedford Forrest and
sentences.zh: 是那些白人至上主义的前邦联分子崩溃了，因为内森·贝德福德·福雷斯特和
zh_words: 内森·贝德福德·福雷斯特

sentences.en: George Gordon lead all their mates to go to Nashville and to see the governor.
sentences.zh: 乔治·戈登带领他们所有的伙伴去纳什维尔面见州长。

sentences.en: And they say, fine, we'll call off the dogs, as it were.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，我们姑且说是收手吧。

sentences.en: There'll be no more violence.
sentences.zh: 不会再有暴力事件了。

sentences.en: And they make a public promise that they will help the authorities maintain the peace and order of the state.
sentences.zh: 他们公开承诺，将协助当局维护州的和平与秩序。

sentences.en: And actually, Gordon, General Gordon, gives a rally in Pulaski, the homeland of the Klan, and he says, in future, we should obey the laws and uphold a spirit of peace and harmony.
sentences.zh: 事实上，戈登，也就是戈登将军，在三K党的发源地普拉斯基举行了一场集会，他说，未来我们应该遵守法律，弘扬和平与和谐的精神。

sentences.en: And actually, at first, it seems to work.
sentences.zh: 而且，起初这似乎奏效了。

sentences.en: So it seems that the tension dissipates.
sentences.zh: 所以紧张局势似乎消散了。

sentences.en: And actually, Brownlow's hard line has paid off.
sentences.zh: 布朗洛的强硬路线确实收到了成效。

sentences.en: However, in the other states of the Confederacy, all this time, Klan support has been building.
sentences.zh: 然而，在邦联的其他州，这段时间以来，对三K党的支持一直在增长。

sentences.en: So the Klan is now heading towards having dens in perhaps a quarter of all counties in the former Confederate South, and probably about 150,000 members.
sentences.zh: 所以，三K党现在在原邦联南部的所有县中，大约四分之一的县里都有分部，成员可能达到了15万人左右。

sentences.en: And don't forget, we're in the summer of 1868 at this point.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，我们现在是在1868年的夏天。

sentences.en: And now the stakes are becoming very high.
sentences.zh: 现在赌注变得非常高了。

sentences.en: Anyway, a reminder, the future of the Republic for the last year or so has been in the hands
sentences.zh: 总之，提醒一下，过去一年左右，共和国的未来一直掌握在

sentences.en: of the radical Republicans in Congress, and the whole Confederacy, with the exception of
sentences.zh: 国会的激进共和党人手中，而整个邦联，除了

sentences.en: Tennessee, has been under military occupation.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州之外，一直处于军事占领之下。

sentences.en: But on the 3rd of November 1868, the American people will have a chance to turn back the clock, because this will be the first presidential election since the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 但在1868年11月3日，美国人民将有机会扭转局面，因为这将是内战以来的第一次总统选举。

sentences.en: So the Republicans, as their candidate, have chosen General Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 所以共和党人选择了尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant.
sentences.zh: 格兰特将军作为他们的候选人。

sentences.en: So he is the ultimate northern war hero, and he is going to stand on an explicit platform of equal and civil political rights for all.
sentences.zh: 他是北方终极的战争英雄，他将站在一个明确的纲领上，即所有人享有平等的公民政治权利。

sentences.en: But the Democrats have chosen, as their candidate, Governor Horatio Seymour of New York.
sentences.zh: 但民主党人选择了纽约州州长霍拉肖·西摩作为他们的候选人。

sentences.en: And he is an outspoken critic of radical reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 他是激进重建政策的直言不讳的批评者。

sentences.en: And his campaign slogan is, and I quote, this is a white man's country, let white men rule.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选口号是，引用一下：这是白人的国家，让白人来统治。

sentences.en: Chilling stuff, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 令人不寒而栗，多米尼克。

sentences.en: And what is to come is going to be even more chilling.
sentences.zh: 而即将到来的事情会更加令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Members of the Rest of History Club can hear that right away, of course, the battle for the future of the South and the fate of the first incarnation of the Ku Klux Klan.
sentences.zh: “历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员当然可以立即听到关于南方未来的斗争，以及三K党第一阶段的命运。

sentences.en: And what you can also hear, if you are a member of the Rest of History Club, are the next two episodes
sentences.zh: 如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员，你还可以听到接下来的两集，

sentences.en: after those two, so episodes three and four, which take the story into the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 也就是第三集和第四集，它们将故事带入了20世纪。

sentences.en: So to join them, if you're not a member, you know what you've got to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你还不是会员，想加入的话，你知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: Restishistory.com and sign up there.
sentences.zh: 去Restishistory.com注册吧。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Thank you, everyone, for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Tom, I have to say, when I look at the sheer sweep and scope of everything we've done on the Rest is History, it starts to look a little bit like the Library of Alexandria,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不得不说，当我审视我们在《历史其余部分》中所做的一切的广度和范围时，它看起来有点像亚历山大图书馆，

sentences.en: doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and of course, the problem with the Library of Alexandria was that it's gone.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，亚历山大图书馆的问题在于它已经消失了。

sentences.en: So whether it was destroyed by the Romans or the Christians or the Muslims or by entropy, who can say?
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是被罗马人、基督徒、穆斯林还是熵所摧毁，谁能说得清呢？

sentences.en: But that is a fate that we do not want to see visited on the Rest is History library.
sentences.zh: 但这正是我们不希望在《历史其余部分》图书馆身上看到的命运。

sentences.en: And so we have built an enormous and exceedingly impressive digital monument to house all our episodes in.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们建造了一座巨大且极其令人印象深刻的数字纪念碑，用来存放我们所有的剧集。

sentences.en: We have.
sentences.zh: 我们确实做到了。

sentences.en: And it is, of course, the official The Rest is History website.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是《历史其余部分》的官方网站。

sentences.en: And I don't know about you, Tom, but when I look at that website, I don't think anything in my life has ever given me greater pleasure.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不知道你怎么想，但当我看到那个网站时，我觉得我生命中没有任何东西比这更让我快乐了。

sentences.en: Well, you'll know, Dominic, I have been so excited about this and particularly about the curated collections.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，多米尼克，我一直对这个感到非常兴奋，特别是关于精选集的部分。

sentences.en: So this features series and episodes organized by theme.
sentences.zh: 它按主题组织了系列和剧集。

sentences.en: So there's ancient history or conquistadors and explorers and so on.
sentences.zh: 比如有古代史、征服者和探险家等等。

sentences.en: And my favorite one is The History of Britain, which goes all the way from Stonehenge up to the fall of Liz Truss in chronological order.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是《英国史》，它按时间顺序从巨石阵一直讲到利兹·特拉斯的下台。

sentences.en: But Tom, I know you love the curated collections, but for me, the real highlight, the jewel in the crown, no less, is the Rest is History archive.
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，我知道你喜欢精选集，但对我来说，真正的亮点，也就是皇冠上的明珠，是《历史其余部分》的档案库。

sentences.en: So it is the complete official catalog of every single episode that we have ever done.
sentences.zh: 它是我们有史以来制作的每一集的完整官方目录。

sentences.en: And it is so unbelievably high tech.
sentences.zh: 而且它拥有令人难以置信的高科技。

sentences.en: It's been built by one of our beloved Athelstans, Matt Povey, with the help of AI.
sentences.zh: 它是由我们敬爱的埃塞尔斯坦成员之一马特·波维在人工智能的帮助下构建的。

sentences.en: So AI, not just in sinister, it does good as well.
sentences.zh: 所以人工智能不仅是邪恶的，它也能做好事。
